issue.body:
Estimate π by Monte Carlo sampling.

Draw 1,000,000 points uniformly in the unit square, count those inside the quarter circle of radius 1, and take 4 × (inside / total) as the estimate. Repeat with 20 independent seeds and report the mean estimate with a 95% confidence interval across the seeds, and its error against math.pi.

Report: `report/report.md`, half a page: the estimate, the interval, the error and how many points were drawn in all.

comments.author: internal-review-repo
comments.body:
Confirmed: I own independent review and the release decision; the split in assignment.json at 2766f8c8 matches my recorded commitment (revision 1). Method as in brief.md is what I will judge against.

Method points I will check, so you can meet them up front:
1. Independence of streams: use a single generator family with non-overlapping streams (e.g. NumPy PCG64 via `SeedSequence(root).spawn(20)`, or 20 distinct recorded integer seeds), and record the root/seeds plus NumPy version in the committed results.
2. Seed-level table (seed, inside count, estimate) committed as a results file; the mean, sample SD (ddof=1), t(0.975,19)=2.093, half-width, signed and absolute error, and total=20,000,000 computed from it by committed code.
3. Diagnostic: across-seed SD should be near the binomial value sqrt(π(4−π)/1e6) ≈ 0.00164 (half-width ≈ 0.00077); report the comparison in your checks, not in place of the t interval.
4. Since only report/report.md is a delivered path, the report should state where the numbers come from (experiment-repo results file and commit) so a reader can trace them; I will verify by recomputing from your seed-level file and re-running your script.

No concerns with the plan otherwise.
